gaps.title: Ensemble/model-disagreement sigma computed then dropped at engine handoff
gaps.what_is_computed: weather_arb._get_forecast builds a skill-weighted multi-model ensemble per city/day and returns (mean, sigma): a BLUE combined sigma from inter-model spread (weather_arb.py:7851 self._ensemble.combine), with low-model-count inflation (×1.40 when n_models<4, line 7855-7856), microclimate sigma adjustment (7867-7880), all logged to forecast_actuals.jsonl as ensemble_sigma (7925).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Only the ensemble MEAN reaches the engine. At weather_arb.py:2016 `ens_mu = fc[_today_s][0]` extracts index [0]; index [1] (sigma) is never read. update_nwp_forecast(slug, hourly) (engine line 553) accepts ONLY hourly temps. The engine then prices spread with a per-(city,month) CONSTANT _peak_sigma_for (stwa_engine.py:1941-1952, used at 1001/1012).
gaps.what_is_lost: Day-specific forecast uncertainty / model disagreement. On high-spread days the pricing sigma stays at the same per-month constant as on consensus days, so bucket probabilities are equally confident regardless of how much the models actually agree. The low-model inflation and microclimate sigma are also discarded.
gaps.evidence: weather_arb.py:2016 (ens_mu = fc[_today_s][0]); weather_arb.py:7851,7855-7856,7911 (sigma computed/returned); stwa_engine.py:553-556 (update_nwp_forecast drops sigma); stwa_engine.py:1012 (_sig = _sig_fc constant)
gaps.test_idea: In forecast_actuals.jsonl bin buckets by ensemble_sigma quantile; compute Brier/realized-WR vs model p_cal per bin. If high-ensemble_sigma days are systematically over/under-confident, the dropped sigma carries signal.

gaps.title: n_models present but never gates STWA engine entry (no-op inflation)
gaps.what_is_computed: _n_models = len(model_values_by_name) and MIN_MODELS_FOR_ENTRY=4 (weather_arb.py:579, 7850).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing for the live STWA engine. The n_models<4 branch only multiplies sigma (which is then dropped, see prior gap) and logs a warning — it does NOT skip/continue (weather_arb.py:7855-7861). The engine never receives n_models, so 'MIN_MODELS_FOR_ENTRY' does not actually gate any STWA entry.
gaps.what_is_lost: Structural reliability signal: days/cities where only 1-3 models responded have structurally underestimated spread, yet still produce full-confidence engine bucket probs at the per-month constant sigma.
gaps.evidence: weather_arb.py:579 (MIN_MODELS_FOR_ENTRY=4), 7855-7861 (only sigma*=1.40 + warning, no continue); engine never references n_models (grep: no n_models in stwa_engine.py)
gaps.test_idea: Join forecast_actuals.jsonl n=len(model_values) against resolution; compare realized calibration of buckets when n_models<4 vs >=4. Confirm the low-n slice is the worse-calibrated tail.

gaps.title: Joint 2N Kalman velocity (x_hat_joint/v_hat_joint) computed live but only logged
gaps.what_is_computed: on_metar runs the full joint position-velocity 2N Kalman update every METAR (stwa_engine.py:806-818), producing x_hat_joint, v_hat_joint, pv_var_joint per city.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing. These three are written ONLY to the stwa_state.jsonl shadow log (lines 1789-1791) and never consumed by any pricer or allocator. The PRIMARY PA_SHRUNK center uses the marginal position x_hat with NO velocity term: _center = _base + PA_SHRUNK_BETA*x_hat (line 1011).
gaps.what_is_lost: The full-information joint estimate of the residual AND its trend. Live pricing ignores velocity entirely; the only velocity used anywhere is cs.v_hat (OLS hack) in the MC/PA SHADOW paths (lines 890, 968), which themselves don't drive the primary decision.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:816-818 (joint computed), 1789-1791 (only logged), 1011 (primary center has no velocity term), 332-334 (fields default 0.0)
gaps.test_idea: From stwa_state.jsonl, regress (resolved_max - ps_center) on v_hat_joint at signal time; if v_hat_joint predicts the residual error, velocity carries unmonetized center-correction.

gaps.title: Primary pricing sigma ignores Kalman posterior variance and cloud regime
gaps.what_is_computed: _forecast_bucket_probs computes p_var (Kalman posterior var, line 852), kriging_pct (855), and regime_mul from REGIME_SIGMA_MUL (cloud sky regime, line 870).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: The PRIMARY PA_SHRUNK spread is _sig = _sig_fc (line 1012) — a per-month constant. regime_mul is applied to the MC/shadow OU sigma (906, 974) but NOT to the PA_SHRUNK _sig. p_var is NOT folded into the pricing CDF width — it only feeds a separate confidence multiplier c_variance (line 1714) and the MC path-init spread (888). So neither current Kalman uncertainty nor cloud regime widens the bucket-probability CDF that drives p_cal.
gaps.what_is_lost: Two state-dependent uncertainty channels. A city with a wide Kalman posterior (sparse/stale obs) or an overcast (CLOUDY ×1.5) regime gets the SAME bucket-prob spread as a tight-posterior sunny city; the extra uncertainty is shunted into a downstream stake multiplier instead of de-sharpening the probabilities themselves.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:1012 (_sig=_sig_fc, no regime_mul, no p_var); 870 vs 906 (regime_mul only on MC sigma); 1714 (p_var only -> c_variance confidence)
gaps.test_idea: Bin stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl p_ps buckets by stwa_state.jsonl kalman_var and regime; check whether realized WR diverges from p_ps within high-var / CLOUDY rows (i.e. those rows are overconfident).

gaps.title: regime_today.json continuous fields (mu/sigma/spread/bias_corr) collapsed to a binary volatile-skip and not seen by the engine
gaps.what_is_computed: regime_detection cron writes regime_today.json with per-city/date {regime, mu, sigma, spread, n_models, bias_corr} (blueprint S2b).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Only the single string field 'regime', via _get_regime (weather_arb.py:68-78), and only as a binary `== 'volatile' -> continue` skip in two LEGACY weather paths (2311, 5363). The live STWA engine path never calls _get_regime; it derives regime from sky_rank (REGIME_FROM_SKY, engine line 272) instead. The continuous mu/sigma/spread/bias_corr are never read.
gaps.what_is_lost: A pre-computed daily ensemble center bias (bias_corr), spread, and continuous uncertainty (sigma/spread) per city — collapsed to one boolean. heatwave/cold_front regimes are treated identically to normal. The engine uses cloud cover as its regime proxy rather than the inter-model-spread regime the cron actually computed.
gaps.evidence: weather_arb.py:68-78 (_get_regime returns only 'regime' string), 2311 & 5363 (binary volatile skip, legacy paths), engine line 272 REGIME_FROM_SKY (engine uses sky regime, never regime_today)
gaps.test_idea: Join regime_today.json sigma/spread/bias_corr to resolution; test whether bias_corr improves the ps_center MBE and whether spread predicts realized bucket-error magnitude beyond the per-month sigma.

gaps.title: kriging_pct (spatial-propagation fraction) computed and logged but never used in decision
gaps.what_is_computed: kriging_pct = 1 - p_var/p_prior (engine line 855) — the fraction of a city's posterior that came from OTHER cities' obs (vs its own), stashed as kriging_pct_last (857) and logged in stwa_signals.jsonl.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing. It is passed through _lp_allocate_city only to be written to the signal log (1123, 1285, 1347, 1597). The confidence score uses p_var directly (c_variance, line 1714) but NOT kriging_pct, so a center estimate that is mostly spatially-inferred (no local obs, higher model risk) is sized identically to a locally-observed one.
gaps.what_is_lost: A provenance/reliability discriminator on the center estimate. High-kriging cities are leaning on neighbor obs + the spatial covariance, which is a different (and likely worse) error regime than a city pinned by its own fresh METAR.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:855-857 (computed/stashed), 1123/1285/1347/1597 (logged only), 1714 (confidence uses p_var not kriging_pct)
gaps.test_idea: Join stwa_signals.jsonl kriging_pct to WEATHER_STWA resolution; bin by kriging_pct and compare realized WR vs p_model — if high-kriging entries underperform their stated edge, it is a usable size/skip gate.

gaps.title: GEV closed-form and PA up-crossing pricers computed every cycle, never drive p_cal
gaps.what_is_computed: Per bucket the engine computes p_mc (MC), p_gev (fitted GEV daily-max, lines 940-956) and p_pa (Rice up-crossing moment propagation, 964-989), all logged to stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Only p_ps (PA_SHRUNK single-Gaussian, line 1031-1032) -> isotonic -> p_cal. p_gev and p_pa are pure shadow; the GEV term correctly models daily-max tail (Gumbel/Frechet) skew that the symmetric Gaussian CDF cannot, but it never blends in. No ensembling of the 4 pricers is done despite all being live.
gaps.what_is_lost: Tail-shape information (the daily max is an extreme-value quantity, not Gaussian). The single symmetric Gaussian CDF systematically mis-prices the upper/lower bucket tails relative to GEV; that correction is computed and discarded.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:940-956 (gev), 964-989 (pa), 1031-1033 (only ps returned), 1689-1699 (all logged for shadow only)
gaps.test_idea: From stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl joined to resolution, compare Brier/log-loss of p_gev and a (p_ps,p_gev) blend vs p_cal on tail buckets; if GEV wins on tails, a tail-bucket blend is +calibration.

gaps.title: BAND_MODE hour-varying gain and explained-variance sigma-shrink are dead code
gaps.what_is_computed: _beta_h (hour-varying anomaly gain 0.30->0.41) and _r2_h (variance explained by morning obs, 0.14->0.30) are measured/defined (lines 243-256) and used to build a tighter, time-aware center+sigma when STWA_BAND_MODE is on (1005-1006: _sig = _sig_fc*sqrt(1-R2_h)).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing — STWA_BAND_MODE=False (line 213), so the engine takes the legacy branch: fixed PA_SHRUNK_BETA=0.30 and fixed _sig=_sig_fc (1011-1012). The measured fact that the morning obs explains MORE of the daily-max by mid-afternoon (so sigma should shrink with time-to-peak) is computed but never applied in the live primary path.
gaps.what_is_lost: Time-to-peak conditioning of BOTH the gain (β rising 0.30->0.41 after 15:00 local) and the spread (sigma should tighten as the obs pins more variance). Live uses a single β and a flat sigma for all intraday hours.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:243-256 (_beta_h/_r2_h), 213 (STWA_BAND_MODE=False), 1002-1012 (BAND branch skipped -> fixed beta/sigma)
gaps.test_idea: Backtest on stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl: recompute p with hour-varying beta_h and sigma*sqrt(1-r2_h) at the row's local hour; compare Brier vs the logged p_ps to see if the dead BAND sigma-shrink improves live-2026 calibration.

gaps.title: Center anchoring is well-handled (contrast, no gap)
gaps.what_is_computed: The ensemble MEAN, the per-(month,hour) NWP bias, learned drift_bias EMA, peak_bias, microclimate mu, and a same-day METAR-trajectory blend ARE all combined into the center: hourly anchored to ens_mu at peak hour (weather_arb.py:2029-2041), _get_mu adds bias+drift (engine 569-575), PA_SHRUNK adds peak_bias + 0.30*x_hat.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: The center is the most thoroughly-monetized stage; multiple bias/drift/microclimate corrections do reach p_cal. Noting here so it is not re-flagged as a gap. The leakage is on the UNCERTAINTY side (sigma/disagreement/velocity), not the center.
gaps.what_is_lost: Minimal on center; the gaps are uncertainty-side.
gaps.evidence: weather_arb.py:2029-2041 (anchor), 7867-7903 (microclimate+METAR blend into mean), stwa_engine.py:569-576 (bias+drift), 1000-1011 (peak_bias+beta*x_hat)
gaps.test_idea: N/A — contrast item documenting the well-handled center path.

gaps.title: Live daily ensemble σ computed then discarded; engine prices with static climatological σ
gaps.what_is_computed: weather_arb._get_forecast → self._ensemble.combine() returns (mean, sigma) = a skill-weighted BLUE ensemble mean and a per-day combined σ across 9-11 models (stwa_engine line 7851-7854). regime_today.json also carries a per-city-day `sigma`, `n_models`, `bias_corr` (rebuilt daily, blueprint §2b).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Only the ensemble MEAN reaches the engine: line 2016 `ens_mu = fc[_today_s][0]` takes index [0] and feeds it as the NWP peak anchor (update_nwp_forecast). The σ at index [1] is dropped. The engine's pricing σ is `_peak_sigma_for` = static per-(city,month) `sigma_monthly` from 2021-24 ASOS (stwa_engine.py:1001, 1941-1947).
gaps.what_is_lost: The day-specific forecast uncertainty. On a high-disagreement day (wide ensemble σ, few models) the engine still prices with the same climatological σ as a calm day, so bucket probs are over-confident exactly when models disagree. n_models and bias_corr never touch pricing either.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:2016 (`ens_mu = fc[_today_s][0]`), stwa_engine.py:7851 (`mean, sigma = self._ensemble.combine`), stwa_engine.py:1001 (`_sig_fc = _peak_sigma_for(...)`), stwa_engine.py:1941 `_peak_sigma_for`; regime_today.json fields regime/sigma/n_models/bias_corr (blueprint §2b).
gaps.test_idea: Join forecast_actuals.jsonl ensemble_sigma to resolution outcomes; bin by ensemble_sigma quartile and check whether realized bucket-hit Brier degrades in the high-σ bin under the static-σ pricer — confirms the daily σ carries calibration signal the engine ignores.

gaps.title: Per-source feed-lead (the NMS edge) is logged but never gates or sizes
gaps.what_is_computed: national_met.py logs per-source obs receipt time and which source won (_log_obs_receipt → obs_receipt.jsonl, recv_ts/source/obs_valid_ts), and stamps `nms_source` on each cached obs (line 683). Blueprint §1a measures ~9-28 min feed-lead over the AWC baseline (commit d73a08d7).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing about source identity or lead reaches the decision. The engine only consumes the merged temp/running_max via on_metar; confidence uses `metar_age` (wall-clock staleness) only, via c_age = exp(-metar_age/τ) (stwa_engine.py:1713). A fill driven by a fast Synoptic obs that AWC has not yet published is sized identically to one on a stale AWC-only obs.
gaps.what_is_lost: The information-advantage window. When we have a fresh fast-feed obs the market has NOT yet seen (because Polymarket MMs price off the slower AWC baseline), that is precisely when our edge is largest — but stake does not scale up, and there is no gate that prefers firing during a confirmed feed-lead window.
gaps.evidence: national_met.py:614-630 (_log_obs_receipt), national_met.py:683 (`nms_source` stamped), stwa_engine.py:1713 (c_age uses metar_age only); blueprint §1a/§4 obs_receipt.jsonl.
gaps.test_idea: Join obs_receipt.jsonl (source, recv_ts) to stwa_signals.jsonl fills and to resolution; compare WR/EV of fills made within N minutes of a non-AWC source lead vs fills on AWC-only obs — quantifies monetizable feed-lead alpha currently unsized.

gaps.title: Isotonic recalibration map is global — one curve for all 49 cities, all regimes, all phases
gaps.what_is_computed: A single monotone map g loaded from config/stwa_isotonic.json as two 1-D arrays (_g, _y) and applied via np.interp(p, _g, _y) to every bucket of every city (stwa_engine.py:1023-1027). Fit pooled on 2024 history.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: This one global p→p_cal map is the win-prob used for edge_yes/edge_no and Kelly (cal_probs → p_use, stwa_engine.py:1366). Tight-σ cities and loose-σ cities, sunny and cloudy, pre-peak and at-peak all share it.
gaps.what_is_lost: Per-city / per-regime / per-phase calibration structure. A model probability of 0.8 means something different in low-σ London vs high-σ SF, and the comment block at stwa_engine.py:96-104 explicitly acknowledges the pooled map 'does NOT know that a tight-σ city's confident bucket genuinely wins more often' — they patched it with a crude w_city Kelly multiplier (YES-only) instead of conditioning the calibration map itself.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:1023-1027 (single np.interp map), stwa_engine.py:1366 (p_use from cal_probs drives edge+Kelly), stwa_engine.py:96-104 (admission the pooled map ignores per-city accuracy), config/stwa_isotonic.json.
gaps.test_idea: Bin stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl (p_ps, p_cal) by city σ-tercile (or sky regime) and compute per-bin reliability vs resolution; if reliability curves diverge across bins, a conditioned isotonic map beats the global one.

gaps.title: Multi-pricer disagreement (MC/GEV/PA vs PA-shrunk) computed every bucket but never used as a model-uncertainty gate
gaps.what_is_computed: For every bucket the engine computes p_mc, p_gev, p_pa, p_ps (PA-shrunk) and logs all four to stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl; gev_probs_last is stored per bucket (stwa_engine.py:949-955, 1685-1696). p_gev is even carried onto the Signal object (line 1588, 1598).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Only p_ps (after the global isotonic g) reaches edge/Kelly. p_gev/p_mc/p_pa are pure shadow. The spread BETWEEN pricers — a free, zero-cost proxy for model/structural uncertainty on that specific bucket — never gates or down-weights a trade.
gaps.what_is_lost: Cross-pricer disagreement as a confidence signal. A bucket where MC says 0.1 and PA-shrunk says 0.6 is structurally uncertain and should be sized down or skipped; today it is treated identically to a bucket where all pricers agree.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:949-955 (gev_probs), stwa_engine.py:1685-1696 (p_mc/p_gev/p_pa/p_ps logged), stwa_engine.py:1588/1598 (p_gev onto Signal but only logged), stwa_engine.py:1366 (only p_use=cal/p_ps used).
gaps.test_idea: From stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl compute |p_ps - p_mc| per bucket; join to resolution and check whether high-disagreement buckets have worse realized calibration / negative EV at the asks we fired — would justify a disagreement gate.

gaps.title: PRICE_FLOOR / NO band are hard binary cutoffs that discard the continuous price-dependent edge curve
gaps.what_is_computed: NO favorite edge and Kelly fraction are computed continuously (edge_no, f_no, stwa_engine.py:1368-1370), but eligibility is a hard window: NO_FLOOR(0.70) ≤ ask_no ≤ NO_CEIL(0.88) (stwa_engine.py:1389) and YES needs ask ≥ PRICE_FLOOR(0.50) (line 1387).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: A binary include/exclude. A NO at ask 0.89 with strong model edge is dropped; one at 0.88 fires at full size. The bands were fit on small resolved-n slices (n=18 in the +EV [0.70,0.85] bin per the inline note line 221-226).
gaps.what_is_lost: The shape of the edge-vs-price relationship. The bands were drawn from a handful of resolved trades and hard-coded; the continuous (price, model-edge) surface is thrown away in favor of step functions, so genuinely +EV fills just outside the band are never taken and the cutoffs are brittle to the small-n they were fit on.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:1387-1393 (binary _yes_price_ok / _no_price_ok gates), stwa_engine.py:220 (PRICE_FLOOR=0.50), stwa_engine.py:227-228 (NO_FLOOR=0.70/NO_CEIL=0.88), stwa_engine.py:221-226 (band fit on n=18/65/111).
gaps.test_idea: Backtest resolved WEATHER_STWA NO fills as a continuous EV(ask, model_edge) regression rather than a band; check whether a smooth size = f(price) Kelly beats the hard window on out-of-sample EV.

gaps.title: `confidence` multiplies the win-prob (shrinks favorites toward 0.5) and double-counts phase/regime already used as gates
gaps.what_is_computed: confidence = c_age·c_variance·c_regime·c_phase (stwa_engine.py:1718), each in (0,1]. It is then applied as p_c = p_win·conf inside Kelly (_kelly_f line 1301; horse-race p*confidence line 1537; _kelly_stake line 1564).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: It both gates (confidence < CONFIDENCE_MIN=0.45 skips the city, line 1720) and sizes (multiplies the win-prob). Multiplying p_win by conf<1 systematically pushes a NO favorite (p_win≈0.85) down toward break-even, understating edge on exactly the proven-EV favorite side; and c_phase/c_regime re-penalize phase and sky-regime that are ALREADY hard gates (phase==PRE_PEAK, REGIME_FIRE).
gaps.what_is_lost: Correct favorite sizing and a clean uncertainty signal. p_win·conf is not a calibrated probability — it conflates 'I am unsure' with 'the event is less likely', biasing Kelly down asymmetrically (hurts high-p favorites most) while the same factors are spent again as binary gates. The intended effect (size down when uncertain) is better expressed via σ-widening, not by deflating p_win.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:1718 (confidence product), stwa_engine.py:1301 (`p_c = p_win * conf`), stwa_engine.py:1537 (`p * confidence`), stwa_engine.py:1564 (_kelly_stake gets 1-p_m * conf), stwa_engine.py:1715-1716 (c_regime/c_phase duplicate the REGIME_FIRE + PRE_PEAK gates).
gaps.test_idea: Recompute historical fired NO signals with conf-as-σ-widening vs conf-as-p-multiplier; compare implied Kelly stake and realized EV per $ on resolved NO favorites to see how much favorite edge the multiplicative form discards.

gaps.title: hot_bust_rates continuous probability collapsed to a binary trigger (and only in a side path, not STWA sizing)
gaps.what_is_computed: hot_bust_rates.json gives a continuous P(actual - GFS ≥ gap) per city/month, queried as _bust_prob (weather_arb.py:6639). hot_bust_observations.jsonl logs daily GFS-d1 errors.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: _bust_prob is thresholded to a boolean trigger_c = _bust_prob ≥ HOT_BUST_MIN_PROB (weather_arb.py:6640) inside the Foehn/upstream-oracle scan — a separate mechanism. The continuous bust probability never sizes a stake and never feeds the live STWA engine's center or σ as a directional GFS-cold-bias prior.
gaps.what_is_lost: A quantified, per-city/month directional bias on the NWP anchor. The STWA engine anchors to the ensemble mean (line 2039) with only a static per-hour `bias` table; the live hot/cold bust rate (a measured systematic GFS error that varies by month) is available but is reduced to an on/off trigger in an unrelated code path.
gaps.evidence: weather_arb.py:6639 (_bust_prob = _hbr().query), weather_arb.py:6640 (binary trigger_c threshold), stwa_engine.py:2039 (engine anchors to ens_mu with static bias only); blueprint §2b hot_bust_rates.json, §4 hot_bust_observations.jsonl.
gaps.test_idea: Regress (actual - ensemble_mu) on hot_bust_rates bust-probability per city-month from hot_bust_observations.jsonl; if a significant slope exists, the engine center is leaving a measurable directional bias-correction on the table.

gaps.title: kriging_pct (spatial-propagation share of the posterior) computed and logged but never gates or sizes
gaps.what_is_computed: kriging_pct = 1 - p_var/p_prior_diag, the fraction of the bucket posterior that came from spatial propagation rather than this city's own obs (stwa_engine.py:855-857). Carried on every Signal (line 1597) and into stwa_signals.jsonl.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing. grep shows kriging_pct is only assigned, passed through, and logged — never compared to a threshold or used as a sizing weight. A bucket prob that is 90% inferred from neighbor cities (no local obs) is sized identically to one anchored on a fresh local METAR.
gaps.what_is_lost: A direct trust signal on the posterior. High kriging_pct means we are leaning on the spatial covariance, not on ground truth for that city — strictly higher uncertainty that should down-weight stake or raise the edge bar, but it is purely diagnostic.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:855-857 (kriging_pct computed), stwa_engine.py:1597 (onto Signal), grep confirms no threshold/sizing use of `.kriging_pct`; stwa_signals.jsonl field kriging_pct (blueprint §3).
gaps.test_idea: Join stwa_signals.jsonl kriging_pct to resolved outcomes; bin by kriging_pct and compare WR/EV — if high-kriging fills underperform, it should gate or shrink stake.

gaps.title: NEG_RISK_ARB (the only calibration-free edge) is disabled in the engine — guaranteed-profit structure not monetized
gaps.what_is_computed: The engine fully computes the neg-risk arb both faces (Σ YES ask < THR and Σ NO ask < N-1) with exhaustivity, depth and budget clamps and writes no_arb_probe.jsonl (stwa_engine.py:1190-1358; weather_arb _no_arb_shadow_probe line 5645).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: STWA_NEG_RISK_ENABLED=False (stwa_engine.py:231) turns the live arb path off — the note says it 'never executed as intended (partial fills on phantom books → -$43.48; 0 fillable arbs in 1947 probe rows).' So the only structurally-sound edge currently contributes nothing live. Noted as category-1 (already modeled / understood) so it is not re-discovered as a new gap.
gaps.what_is_lost: Nothing new conceptually — but the gap is execution, not modeling: the probe shows 0 fillable arbs largely because depth/real-book is only fetched for a screened subset (weather_arb.py:5584-5639). Worth flagging that the calibration-free edge is gated off on execution grounds, so all live risk currently rides on the unproven directional NO calibration.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:231 (STWA_NEG_RISK_ENABLED=False), stwa_engine.py:1190-1358 (arb faces computed), weather_arb.py:5645 (_no_arb_shadow_probe), weather_arb.py:5584-5639 (depth fetched only for screened cities).
gaps.test_idea: From no_arb_probe.jsonl count rows where all_legs_fillable AND real_arb>0 after the full top-5 book fetch (not proxy); if any exist, the disablement is over-broad and the calibration-free edge is recoverable.

gaps.title: Day-specific NWP ensemble dispersion never reaches the pricer (pricing sigma is static climatology)
gaps.what_is_computed: weather_arb._get_forecast computes a per-day across-model spread and an ensemble_sigma via WeightedEnsemble.combine (ensemble_weights.py:179-198: sigma=GAMMA*1/sqrt(Sum 1/sigma_k^2), floored). Both raw spread and ensemble_sigma are logged to forecast_actuals.jsonl (weather_arb.py:7919-7926). Raw across-model spread varies 0.2-15C (median 3.5C) across 41,273 logged forecasts.
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Nothing day-specific. The live PA_SHRUNK pricer (stwa_engine.py:1001,1012 _sig=_sig_fc) prices every bucket with _peak_sigma_for() = a STATIC per-(city,month) sigma_monthly from config/stwa_peak_calib.json (e.g. chicago June = 0.614C always). calib_verify.py:6 states outright: ensemble_sigma 'the live pricer does NOT use'.

This is the inverse-variance BLUE-minimum sigma assuming the historical per-model error variances, NOT the actual disagreement among today's model forecasts.

gaps.evidence: logs/weather/forecast_actuals.jsonl (854 city-day keys, snapshots/key median 35); revision |mu_last-mu_first| p90=2.39C, >2C 15.3%; consumed only at weather_arb.py:2976-2983 for scan cadence
gaps.test_idea: Bucket resolved trades by intraday revision magnitude at entry; test whether realized WR/Brier degrades on high-revision days vs the model's stated probability.

gaps.title: Humidity (dew) correction applies a dewpoint-departure coefficient against NWP AIR TEMPERATURE
gaps.what_is_computed: stwa_fit_params.py:192-201 fits alpha_humidity per (city,month) as OLS slope of residual on (dew_c - dew_nwp_c) — observed dew minus NWP DEW point. alpha is populated and nonzero for all 51 cities (e.g. amsterdam month-by-month up to 0.43).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: Live, stwa_engine.py:664-669 applies mu_corrected += alpha*(dew_c - nwp_dew), but nwp_dew = self._nwp_cache.get(city).get(hour_utc) and _nwp_cache holds hourly_temps (NWP TEMPERATURE), set at stwa_engine.py:553-556 / update_nwp_forecast. So the predictor is (observed_dew - NWP_air_temp), not (observed_dew - NWP_dew).
gaps.what_is_lost: A correctly-specified humidity correction. The applied predictor is offset by the NWP temp-dew spread (typically 5-15C), so a coefficient fit on dew-departure multiplies a quantity ~an order of magnitude larger and wrong-signed — the dew signal is effectively garbled rather than corrective. The infrastructure (alpha fit + dew obs + dew_nwp_c column in stwa_nwp.parquet) exists but the live wiring grabs the wrong cache.
gaps.evidence: stwa_fit_params.py:197 (x = sub['dew_c'] - sub['dew_nwp_c']); stwa_engine.py:553-556 (_nwp_cache = hourly_temps); stwa_engine.py:665-669 (nwp_dew pulled from temp cache); config/stwa_params.json alpha_humidity nonzero all 51 cities
gaps.test_idea: Replay engine with corrected nwp_dew cache (separate dew forecast) and measure residual reduction vs current on stwa_asos.parquet held-out.

gaps.title: Continuous sky info collapsed to a 3-level regime in the engine sigma path
gaps.what_is_computed: stwa_asos.parquet carries sky_rank (0-4) and the nowcast path uses a continuous sky_factor / cirrus-adjusted f_sky. The cirrus adjustment (met_adjustments) reclassifies high-transmittance clouds and DOES feed mu_final live (weather_arb.py:7667-7721).
gaps.what_reaches_decision: In the Kalman engine path, sky_rank is mapped to only 3 regimes (REGIME_FROM_SKY: 0/1->SUNNY, 2->PARTLY, 3/4->CLOUDY, stwa_engine.py:272) driving a coarse sigma multiplier {1.0,1.2,1.5} (line 274) and a fire/no-fire gate (CLOUDY never fires, line 273/1640). FEW vs SCT vs BKN distinctions and the continuous sky_factor are flattened.
gaps.what_is_lost: Gradation between clear and overcast. The nowcast path already has a continuous f_sky (0-1) with cirrus correction; the engine sigma/gate path throws it to 3 buckets, so two days with sky_factor 0.35 and 0.95 can land in the same regime and same sigma multiplier.
gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:272-274 (REGIME_FROM_SKY 3-level, REGIME_SIGMA_MUL {SUNNY:1.0,PARTLY:1.2,CLOUDY:1.5}); stwa_engine.py:642,870,1640; vs continuous f_sky at weather_arb.py:7667-7721
gaps.test_idea: Regress residual variance on continuous sky_factor vs 3-bucket regime; compare explained variance to see how much sigma resolution is lost.

gaps.title: Joint 2N Kalman velocity (v_hat_joint) computed and logged but never priced
gaps.what_is_computed: The full joint (X,V) 2N Kalman over all cities is run live and per-city x_hat_joint, v_hat_joint, pv_var_joint are computed (stwa_engine.py:816-818) and logged to stwa_state.jsonl.

gaps.evidence: stwa_engine.py:816-818 (cs.x_hat_joint/v_hat_joint/pv_var_joint set); logged only; live mu_kalman uses non-joint path; CLAUDE.md MATHEMATICAL CORE notes joint runs 'in shadow'

gaps.title: Fast-NMS feed-lead over AWC measured but provably not monetized
gaps.what_is_computed: obs_receipt.jsonl logs per-source recv_ts vs obs_valid_ts (Stage-0, commit d73a08d7, deployed only ~1 day ago). national_met.py merges all sources freshest-per-station into _icao_metar_cache.

gaps.title: latent_heat (precip suppression) adjustment never activates

quants.gap_title: Humidity correction multiplies alpha (fit on dewpoint-departure) by the wrong cached quantity — NWP air temp, not NWP dew — doubling forecast-center MSE
quants.claim_tested: stwa_engine.py:665 pulls nwp_dew from _nwp_cache, which only ever holds NWP AIR temperatures (set in update_nwp_forecast, line 553-556). So line 669 computes alpha*(dew_c - temp_nwp_c) instead of the intended alpha*(dew_c - dew_nwp_c) on which alpha was fit (stwa_fit_params.py:197). The applied predictor is offset by the NWP dewpoint depression (~5-15C). Claim: the correct wiring carries monetizable predictive value AND the live buggy wiring actively degrades the forecast center.
quants.method: Joined data/stwa_asos.parquet (temp_c, dew_c) to data/stwa_nwp.parquet (temp_nwp_c, dew_nwp_c) on (city, time_utc), collapsing multi-model NWP to per-(city,time) mean -> 669,515 rows. Target = resid_raw = temp_c - temp_nwp_c (the air-temp forecast error the correction is meant to reduce, per fit_params.py:145). Reconstructed both predictors: x_correct=dew_c-dew_nwp_c (fit basis), x_buggy=dew_c-temp_nwp_c (live wiring). Evaluated on 2024 (n=380,761) using the LIVE production alpha coefficients from config/stwa_params.json, and separately with an honest OOS refit (train<=2023, test=2024). Also isolated the daily-max hour (idxmax of temp_c per city-date, n=16,055 city-days) to measure center mispricing at the resolution-relevant point.
quants.key_numbers: NWP dew depression (temp_nwp-dew_nwp): mean 6.21C, p90 13.6C -> the offset injected. x_buggy mean -6.31/std 5.76 vs x_correct mean -0.10/std 1.71. LIVE-params 2024 residual MSE: no-correction 2.4298; correct wiring 2.2725 (-6.47%, helps 39/51 cities); BUGGY live wiring 4.8825 (+100.9%, hurts 45/51 cities). Worst cities under bug (OOS refit): nyc +363%, austin +341%, denver +336%, dallas +117%, los-angeles +111%. corr(x_correct,resid)=-0.025 weak but corr(x_buggy,resid)=+0.114 wrong-signed spurious. At daily-max hour the spurious center shift (buggy-correct) is abs-mean 1.70C, 70% of city-days >0.5C, 52% >1.0C; implied avg |win-prob mispricing| at sigma=1.05 ~0.62.
quants.signal_strength: strong — the correct wiring cuts forecast-center MSE 6.5% (n=380,761, helps 39/51 cities) and removing the bug eliminates a +101% MSE inflation; both far exceed noise. Daily-max center is moved >0.5C on 70% of 16,055 city-days.
quants.caveats: (1) Bug confirmed in code: stwa_engine.py:553-556 caches air temps; line 665 reads nwp_dew from that same cache; line 669 forms alpha*(dew_c - air_temp). config/stwa_nwp.parquet has a dedicated dew_nwp_c column that the live engine never loads. (2) This is a residual/center analysis on ASOS history, NOT a resolved-trade Brier/PnL — live model-NO n is only ~12 (trend-only, below n>=100), so I cannot quote realized EV/contract; the monetization path is: fixing the center directly re-prices every favorite-NO bucket (STWA_REGULAR_NO_ENABLED=True, PRICE_FLOOR 0.50, EDGE_MIN 0.04) that this center feeds. (3) Two correct fixes exist and both should be tested: wire a real dew forecast cache, OR (cheaper/safer) disable the term — note correct wiring only gives -6.5% and the bug gives +101%, so even setting alpha_humidity to 0 recovers most of the lost ground with zero new plumbing. (4) Look-ahead: 2024 is in-sample for the live params (fit train_end=2024), which if anything understates the buggy harm; the OOS train<=2023/test=2024 split corroborates (correct -1% to -6%, buggy +39% all-city). (5) Non-US per-city OOS deltas showed 0% only because my <=2023 refit lacked >=100 obs/month for those cities; live params are nonzero for 50/51 cities so the bug fires city-wide.

quants.gap_title: Sky-cloud regime sigma multiplier reaches only the SHADOW MC pricer, not the live PA_SHRUNK distribution that sizes NO
quants.claim_tested: (a) Code: REGIME_SIGMA_MUL (SUNNY 1.0 / PARTLY 1.2 / CLOUDY 1.5) is applied to MC sigma (stwa_engine.py:870,906,974) but NOT to the live PA_SHRUNK sigma (stwa_engine.py:1012 _sig=_sig_fc), so the priced/NO-sizing distribution ignores cloud-conditioned uncertainty. (b) Empirical: is the discarded cloud signal predictive — i.e. is PA_SHRUNK (p_ps) overconfident on CLOUDY days relative to MC (p_mc), and would porting regime_mul into PA_SHRUNK monetizably improve the model-NO path?
quants.method: Built join over 2026-05-29..06-04 (overlap of pricer logs + gamma resolution; gamma actuals stop 06-04). Resolution truth = wu_high_c per (city_slug, valid_day) from logs/weather/forecast_actuals_gamma.jsonl (831 actual rows, 50 cities). Per (city,day,lo,hi) took the LAST PRE_PEAK row from logs/shadow/hot/<day>/stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl (carries both p_mc=regime_mul-applied and p_ps=no-regime_mul). Sky regime per (city,day) = modal regime over the day from stwa_state.jsonl (the only shadow log carrying the regime label; pricer_eval does NOT log regime). YES outcome = 1 if lo<=wu_high_c<hi. Joined n=3237 bucket-day rows (525 dropped, no gamma truth; 0 dropped for regime). Two-proportion z-test on confident-NO surprise rate; Brier and mean-vs-realized by regime and p-bin. Code verification: grep regime_mul -> stwa_engine.py lines 274/703/870/906/974 (all MC/obs paths) vs line 1012 PA_SHRUNK using bare _sig_fc.
quants.key_numbers: Code claim CONFIRMED: regime_mul never touches PA_SHRUNK sigma (line 1012). Signal IS real: among model-confident-NO buckets (p_ps<0.05), surprise-YES rate = 6.71% CLOUDY (n=700) vs 4.33% SUNNY (n=1847), z=2.47, p=0.0136. Whole NO-candidate region (p_ps<0.50): CLOUDY realized YES 7.43% vs mean p_ps 1.25% (understates YES by 6.2pp); SUNNY realized 5.40% vs mean 1.88% (understates 3.5pp) -> model is more overconfident on cloudy days. BUT the proposed fix is REFUTED: p_mc (which DOES apply the 1.5x CLOUDY multiplier) is statistically indistinguishable from p_ps -- CLOUDY NO-region Brier p_ps 0.07216 vs p_mc 0.07149 (delta +0.00067); CLOUDY understatement p_ps 0.0618 vs p_mc 0.0594; confident-NO surprise p_ps<0.05 6.71% vs p_mc<0.05 6.56%. The 1.5x lifts mean tail prob only 0.0125->0.0135, closing ~2% of a 600% gap. Overall Brier: p_mc 0.09623 vs p_ps 0.09822 (n=3237). Monetization ceiling: excess CLOUDY surprise 2.38pp -> ~-2.4c/$1 NO notional EV drag on cloudy-day fills.
quants.signal_strength: moderate — cloud-conditioned NO overconfidence is statistically significant (CLOUDY confident-NO surprise 6.71% vs SUNNY 4.33%, z=2.47 p=0.0136, n=700/1847; NO-region understatement 6.2pp cloudy vs 3.5pp sunny). But the CODE's existing regime_mul does NOT capture it: p_mc≈p_ps everywhere it matters.
quants.caveats: 1) The gap's prescribed fix (port REGIME_SIGMA_MUL into PA_SHRUNK at line 1012) is REFUTED by direct evidence: p_mc already carries the 1.5x and is indistinguishable from p_ps (Brier delta 0.00067, understatement gap 0.0024). Multiplying a near-zero deep-tail sigma by 1.5x cannot lift a 0.0125 mean to a realized 0.074 — a ~6x lift / regime-conditioned isotonic haircut or additive NO-tail floor is required, not the existing multiplier. So 'port regime_mul' would NOT monetize. 2) Both pricers are massively tail-overconfident on BOTH regimes (understate YES 3.5-6.2pp), so the dominant edge-leak is general deep-tail NO overconfidence, not specifically the cloud channel. 3) PRICE_FLOOR=0.50 + EDGE_MIN=0.04 means model-NO mostly fires on buckets with NO ask>=0.50 (YES ask<=0.50); the deepest-tail p<0.05 buckets (where the cloud surprise is largest) have NO ask~1.0 and largely cannot be bought as favorites, capping the realized exposure to this leak. 4) Look-ahead: regime is the day's MODAL regime (uses full-day state); a live fix must use regime AS OF the PRE_PEAK decision. CLOUDY n at PRE_PEAK=811 buckets across 7 days clears n>=100 but is only 7 city-days deep per the local resolution constraint — treat the magnitude as trend-grade. 5) Gamma actuals end 06-04, so the freshest 4 days of pricer logs are unjoinable.

quants.gap_title: kriging_pct (spatial-propagation share of state) computed and logged but never sizes/widens the distribution
quants.claim_tested: That kriging_pct carries predictive value: high-kriging cities (state inferred from neighbors, no fresh local METAR) underperform at the same p_var/ask and should be gated or sigma-inflated. Tested by joining stwa_signals.jsonl kriging_pct to Gamma daily-max resolution and binning NO win-rate / EV by kriging quartile, controlling for ask.
quants.method: Join: NO-direction rows from logs/shadow/hot/{2026-05-29..06-02}/stwa_signals.jsonl (the only days overlapping the Gamma resolution window, which ends 2026-06-04). Mapped each signal ts to its city-LOCAL valid_day via STATIONS[city].tz, joined to wu_high_c in logs/weather/forecast_actuals_gamma.jsonl. NO wins if wu_high_c not in bucket [lo,hi). Deduped to one entry per (city,bucket,valid_day) keeping the last intraday signal -> n=113 deduped NO entries (9,540 raw NO signals, 583 with no resolution). EV/share = (1-ask) if NO wins else -ask. Cross-checked realized PnL via logs/trades.jsonl WEATHER/STWA BUY_NO (n=113, but those carry no kriging_pct field, so only a sanity check). stwa_engine.py:855 definition, :1123/:1285/:1348/:1597 logging-only; grep confirms no use in _kelly_f or sigma path.
quants.key_numbers: Raw corr(kriging_pct, no_win)=+0.390 (n=113) looks promising, BUT corr(kriging_pct, ask)=+0.536 and corr(ask, no_win)=+0.633. PARTIAL corr(kriging_pct, no_win | ask)=+0.078 -- the apparent signal is almost entirely a proxy for the market ask. Ask-controlled bands contradict each other: ask[0.10,0.30] hi-kp WR=0.33 vs lo-kp 0.50; ask[0.30,0.55] hi-kp WR=0.91 vs lo-kp 0.60 (no consistent direction, n=6-11 each). DECISIVE: kriging_pct range over 9,540 NO signals is only [0.27,0.80], median 0.488; signals with kp>0.85 ('90%-kriged') = 0 (0.0%); kp>0.75 = 5 (0.1%). The 'state mostly guessed from neighbors' regime the gap warns about never occurs. Live-eligible slice (ask>=0.50, the actual NO buy path under PRICE_FLOOR) = only n=15. Realized trades.jsonl BUY_NO cross-check: n=113, WR 0.54, net -$85.72.
quants.signal_strength: none -- raw corr +0.39 collapses to partial corr +0.078 after controlling for ask; and the high-kriging regime the gap hypothesizes (kp>0.85) has 0 occurrences in 9,540 signals (observed max 0.80, median 0.49)
quants.caveats: (1) Premise refuted at source: kriging_pct never reaches the 'mostly inferred' levels the gap describes -- own-obs always retains >~20% of posterior weight (p_var never below ~0.27 of prior diag), so there is no underpriced no-local-confirmation cohort to gate. (2) Direction is also opposite the hypothesis: raw, higher kriging -> HIGHER (not lower) NO win-rate, because kriging_pct co-moves with ask, and ask is the dominant predictor. (3) Sample is fatally small for a decision: live-eligible (ask>=0.50) n=15 << n>=100 house gate; deduped pool n=113 only by including sub-floor asks that are not actually traded. (4) Resolution join uses Gamma wu_high_c (the validated UMA-equivalent oracle) but kriging_pct lives ONLY in shadow signals, so it cannot be joined to realized trades.jsonl PnL -- this is a shadow-signal proxy, not realized fills. (5) Look-ahead: signals are logged pre-resolution, so no contamination, but the same (city,bucket,day) appears many times intraday; dedup-to-last is a choice that could bias kriging toward late-day (more-kriged) values. (6) Possible future utility only IF the spatial Kalman is ever reweighted to allow >0.85 kriging (e.g. during widespread METAR outages) -- not the current regime. CONCLUSION: do not build a kriging_pct gate or sigma-inflator; no monetizable edge in the logged data.

quants.gap_title: Live cross-model forecast dispersion discarded; sigma uses static skill-matrix climatology
quants.claim_tested: That replacing the static per-(city,model,month) BLUE skill-matrix sigma in WeightedEnsemble.combine (ensemble_weights.py:186-191) with a sigma scaled by today's live 7-model inter-model dispersion improves bucket-probability calibration (Brier/log-loss) against resolution, i.e. high-dispersion days are genuinely more uncertain and that signal is monetizable.
quants.method: Imported the actual WeightedEnsemble class and called combine() to reproduce the live (mu, sigma_static) per snapshot. Joined the LAST forecast snapshot per (city, valid_day) from logs/weather/forecast_actuals.jsonl (41,273 forecast rows, 854 city-days) to whole-degree resolution truth wu_high_c in logs/weather/forecast_actuals_gamma.jsonl (831 actuals). n=484 joined city-days across 48 cities (max 15/city, 26 cities with n>=10). For each city-day priced whole-degree buckets [c-0.5,c+0.5] for c in round(mu)+/-3 via normal CDF (3,388 bucket evals), scored Brier + log-loss of bucket-resolved-YES. Compared sigma_static against k*live_dispersion (sample std of the 7 model_values), max(static,k*disp), global rescale g*static, and a g=1.2*static dispersion-ratio tilt.
quants.key_numbers: STATIC (live pipeline) Brier 0.09400, LogLoss 0.32188. Pure k*live_dispersion WORSE at every k: best k=0.8 Brier 0.09875 (delta +0.00475), k=1.0 0.10021, k=1.4 0.10448. max(static,k*disp) best at k=0.6 Brier 0.09581 (still worse). corr(live_disp, |actual-mu|)=0.139 vs corr(static_sig, |actual-mu|)=0.289 — static predicts error BETTER than dispersion. Real fix is a level inflation not dispersion: g=1.2*static Brier 0.09378, LogLoss 0.31271 (improves both); adding any dispersion tilt on top of g=1.2 monotonically hurts (tilt a=0.15 LL 0.31441, a=0.30 0.31745, a=0.50 0.32363). Static sigma under-dispersed: z-std 1.58, frac|z|>2 = 0.153 (expect 0.05). Conditional grain: high-disp tercile z-rms 1.68 vs low-disp 1.34 (n=162 each).
quants.signal_strength: weak — corr(live_disp,|error|)=0.139 exists but is dominated by static_sig (0.289); every dispersion-scaled sigma loses to static on Brier (best regression +0.0048). The only directionally-real conditional effect (high-disp z-rms 1.68 vs 1.34) does not survive into a usable sigma multiplier (all tilt strengths hurt).
quants.caveats: REFUTES the gap's core claim. (1) Live dispersion carries some information about error magnitude but LESS than the static skill-matrix sigma already encodes; substituting it degrades calibration. (2) The auditor's framing that static sigma is 'near-constant' is wrong across the joined sample: static-sigma std=1.53 across city-days actually EXCEEDS live-dispersion std=0.63 (because per-city/month climatology varies a lot city-to-city). (3) There IS a real, separate, monetizable finding hiding here: the static sigma is under-dispersed (z-std 1.58), and a flat global inflation g~1.2 improves LogLoss 0.3219->0.3127 and Brier 0.0940->0.0938 — but that is a constant GAMMA bump (currently GAMMA=1.30 at ensemble_weights.py:30, applied before the asos floor), not a dispersion signal. Recommend testing raising effective sigma inflation rather than wiring in live dispersion. (4) Look-ahead: used the last snapshot per city-day (closest to resolution, what the bot prices late intraday); resolution is whole-degree gamma truth, no leakage. (5) n=484 clears the n>=100 bar. (6) Bucket grid is symmetric +/-3 around mu and ignores the running-max hard floor, so absolute Brier is a relative-comparison metric, not the live pipeline's exact number — the static-vs-dispersion ordering is the load-bearing result and is unambiguous.

quants.gap_title: Forecast revision velocity (|mu_last - mu_first|) predicts forecast error and model overconfidence, but never widens the priced sigma
quants.claim_tested: That intraday/lifecycle forecast revision magnitude carries predictive uncertainty information that the STWA probability estimate discards: a city-day whose ensemble_mu is still swinging is far less certain than its static ensemble_sigma admits, and the model is therefore overconfident exactly on high-revision days — including on the live NO-favorite path.
quants.method: Joined three real logs. (1) Revision per (city_slug, valid_day) from logs/weather/forecast_actuals.jsonl: grouped all forecast snapshots, sorted by ts_utc, revmag = |ensemble_mu_last - ensemble_mu_first|; 854 city-day keys, snapshots span mean 35.8h / p90 45.9h (full multi-day forecast lifecycle, not just intraday). (2) Resolution truth wu_high_c from logs/weather/forecast_actuals_gamma.jsonl (831 actuals, provenance gamma_backfill). (3) Joined 484 city-days (>=2 snaps + resolution). Model bucket prob computed with the pricer's own Gaussian-CDF-over-whole-degree primitive from final mu + final ensemble_sigma. Verified consumption gap by grep: ensemble_sigma written at weather_arb.py:7925; the only cross-snapshot mu-delta consumer is the scan-cadence switch at weather_arb.py:2976-2983 (required_runs), never the sigma/probability.
quants.key_numbers: n=484 joined. Revision stats reproduce auditor: mean 0.98C, p90 2.39C, >1C 34.7%, >2C 15.3%. Calibration gap (model_p_mode - realized WR) is monotone in revision: rev<=0.5C gap -0.121 (n=188, underconfident); 0.5-1C -0.003 (n=101); 1-2C +0.088 (n=102); >2C +0.358 (n=85, p_mode=0.440 vs WR=0.082 -- massively overconfident). Combined rev>1C: n=187, model_p_mode 0.414 vs WR 0.203. corr(revmag, |mu_final-actual|)=+0.421 (Spearman +0.278) -- revision robustly predicts final error; NOT a snapshot-count artifact (corr(n_snaps,revmag)=0.22). Smoking gun: corr(revmag, final_sigma) = -0.235 -- sigma TIGHTENS on high-revision days (high-rev sigma 0.92 vs low-rev 2.09). Fit-free fix: full-distribution multiclass Brier improves from 0.8226 to 0.7891 (delta -0.0335, ~4.1% relative) with sigma -> sigma + 0.5*revmag, no params tuned on resolution. Monetization: NO-favorite hazard -- a bucket >=2deg from mu (model treats near-impossible, the path buys NO at ask>=0.50) actually resolves YES 32.6% on rev>1 days (n=187) vs 13.5% on rev<=1 (n=289).
quants.signal_strength: strong -- monotone calibration-gap collapse from -0.12 to +0.36 across revision bins, corr(revmag,final_error)=+0.42, and the model's sigma moves the WRONG way (corr -0.235); >2C bin n=85, combined rev>1 n=187 (>=100 = real per house rules).
quants.caveats: (1) Resolution truth is gamma_backfill wu_high_c with ts_utc null; cannot reconstruct the exact mu at the moment each NO fill was placed, so this measures the model's distribution quality, not a perfect replay of executed fills. (2) Snapshots span ~36-46h, so 'revision' is the full forecast-convergence path, not strictly within-the-trading-day; the signal at entry time is the partial revision-so-far, which will be weaker than the full-lifecycle revmag used here -- treat the Brier delta as an upper bound until tested on as-of-entry revision. (3) ensemble_sigma already varies within day (range mean 0.52) but moves opposite to revision, so the lever is real and additive, not redundant. (4) The simple sigma+0.5*revmag rule is illustrative; the production fix should re-fit the isotonic map conditioned on revision bin, and crucially gate/skip the NO-favorite buy when as-of-entry revision >1C (the 32.6% YES-resolution hazard directly poisons the PRICE_FLOOR=0.50 NO harvest). (5) Spearman (+0.28) is lower than Pearson (+0.42), so a few high-rev outliers carry weight -- the >2C bin is the dominant driver and should be validated as it grows past n=100.

quants.gap_title: Per-city daily-max center bias is NOT zero-mean — frozen-2024 peak_bias drifted and the hourly drift_bias EMA fails to correct it at the peak (refutes "mean is handled well")
quants.claim_tested: Auditor category-1 claim: "Nothing is lost on the center/bias axis; center error e=center−actual is approximately zero-mean per (city,hour), so the mean is reasonably conditioned and effort should go only to sigma." I tested whether residual per-city center bias survives the drift_bias + peak_bias machinery and whether correcting it is monetizable OOS.
quants.method: Joined live forecasts (logs/weather/forecast_actuals.jsonl, event=forecast, final_snapshot ensemble_mu) to realized daily-max actuals (max running_max_c per city-day over logs/shadow/hot/*/metar_lockout.jsonl) via analysis/weather/skill_scorecard.py loaders + emos_recal.py. Engine center reconstructed as ensemble_mu + config/stwa_peak_calib.json peak_bias (the actual live center per stwa_engine.py:1000). Cross-checked against an independent live reconstruction (p_ps-weighted bucket midpoint from stwa_pricer_eval.jsonl). Compared the live daily-max error sign to the applied drift_bias (data/stwa_city_state.json, stwa_engine.py:574 _get_mu / :675). Monetization: split-half per city (sorted by day), learned bias on fold-1, applied shrunk correction to fold-2, scored MAE and closed-form CRPS (EMOS-inflated σ×1.606).
quants.key_numbers: Aggregate center bias −0.26°C (looks fine, masks cancellation). Per-city bias is large and sign-stable: seoul −2.45, istanbul −1.72, tokyo −1.67, miami −1.25, jeddah −1.15, guangzhou −1.05, kuala-lumpur −1.20, seattle +1.84, chicago +0.95 (n=4–11/city, 421 city-days, 46 cities). Split-half sign-match 28/41 cities, cross-half bias corr +0.46. The frozen 2024 peak_bias is WRONG-SIGN for 2026 in several: seoul +0.40 (live −2.45), kuala-lumpur +0.43 (live −1.20), guangzhou +0.55 (live −1.05), taipei +0.62 (live −0.91). drift_bias only opposes the daily-max error in 21/40 cities (coin flip), is too small (±0.1–0.6 vs up to −2.45), and is EMPTY for seoul (worst city). OOS shrunk (k=0.5) per-city bias correction: MAE 0.92→0.86 (all), 1.07→0.87 high-bias subset (n=57); CRPS 0.684→0.649 (+5.2%, n=202) all, 0.792→0.655 (+17.4%) on |bias|≥0.8 subset.
quants.signal_strength: moderate — OOS CRPS +5.2% pooled (n=202), +17.4% on the high-bias subset (n=57); split-half sign-match 28/41 and bias-corr +0.46 confirm persistence, but per-city n=4–11 is trend-only by house rules so only the pooled/shrunk correction clears the bar.
quants.caveats: (1) k=1.0 (full) correction HURTS (MAE 0.92→0.96) — only the SHRUNK k=0.5 helps, because per-city bias magnitude regresses ~50% across halves; ship as shrinkage, never full. (2) Actuals use METAR-proxy running_max_c, NOT provenance-clean official_running_max_c — emos_recal flags seoul/tokyo/jeddah/istanbul/miami/guangzhou/kuala-lumpur as ⚠bias=station/oracle mismatch, so part of the largest biases may be wrong-station oracle artifacts a μ-shift would mask rather than fix; but the +5.2% effect holds across all 41 cities, not just oracle-suspect ones. (3) Per-city n is small (days), so this must be a pooled/shrunk EMOS correction, not 41 independent per-city fits. (4) Forecast-snapshot lead times vary; final_snapshot mitigates but doesn't eliminate lead-time mixing. (5) This is a center improvement; the actual dollar edge still rides through the isotonic recal map and the NO-only PRICE_FLOOR=0.50 gate — net EV/contract not directly measured here.

quants.gap_title: Marine/cirrus mu-adjustments are shadow-logged but NEVER reach a live trading decision (and carry no measurable predictive lift)
quants.claim_tested: Auditor premise: "marine sea-breeze multiplier and cirrus reclassification DO reach live mu (handled — contrast case); nothing material lost." Tested both (a) the plumbing claim that mu_final reaches a live decision, and (b) whether the marine damping improves accuracy vs the undamped baseline on resolved city-days.
quants.method: Traced consumers of the adjusted mu. mu_final is produced in _nowcast_max (weather_arb.py:7592-7721; marine block 7667-7686). Its only trading-decision consumers are _intraday_scan (callsite 5384) and no_side_arb.py:155. _intraday_scan is gated by INTRADAY_ENABLED=False (weather_arb.py:394, disabled 2026-05-24; loop guard at 3117-3118). no_side_arb (WEATHER_NOSIDE) has no live-loop wiring grep hit and only 5 lifetime trades in logs/trades.jsonl. The live engine path stwa_engine.py (PA_SHRUNK center = NWP_peak + peak_bias + beta*x_hat) has ZERO marine/cirrus/wind/f_sky/mean_rise references. _poll_metars (live, called at 3105) calls _nowcast_max at 4936 but only logs est_max/p_nc and stores in meta — never sizes. Validation join: parsed logs/shadow/met_adjustments.jsonl (7665 rows, ts 2026-05-21..06-07), kept marine-active rows (5260), grouped to 21 (city,day), took the last obs before peak, joined on normalized (city_slug, valid_day) to resolution truth wu_high_c from logs/weather/forecast_actuals.jsonl + forecast_actuals_gamma.jsonl (978 truth city-days). 18 marine city-days joined; compared |mu_baseline - real| vs |mu_final - real|.
quants.key_numbers: met_adjustments: total_delta nonzero 91.5%, |delta|>0.5C 14.6%, range [-2.67,+2.74] (confirms auditor stats). Validation n=18 marine city-days joined to truth. MAE baseline (no marine) = 0.882C; MAE final (marine-damped) = 0.893C -> damping makes it slightly WORSE. Mean signed error baseline -0.189C, final -0.453C (damping overcorrects downward). Directional test: of 12 days where marine multiplier damped mu down, realized was below baseline pred only 7/12 (= chance). On the 6 |delta|>0.3 days, final closer 4/6 but MAE 0.634->0.669 (worse). Plumbing: INTRADAY_ENABLED=False since 2026-05-24; 9 lifetime WEATHER_INTRADAY trades, 5 WEATHER_NOSIDE; live engine stwa_engine.py marine/cirrus refs = 0.
quants.signal_strength: none — MAE gets worse with the adjustment (0.882->0.893), directional hit-rate 7/12 = chance; and the path it feeds (INTRADAY) is disabled so it reaches no live decision regardless
quants.caveats: REFUTES the auditor's "handled/contrast" framing on two counts. (1) Plumbing: the adjustment does NOT reach live mu — its only decision-consumers (_intraday_scan, no_side_arb) are disabled/dead; the live PA_SHRUNK engine never sees it. This is a category-5 gap (computed, shadow-logged to met_adjustments.jsonl, discarded), not a contrast case. (2) Even if re-plumbed, the signal shows no validated lift. SAMPLE SIZE is anecdote-tier: n=18 overall, n=6 for meaningful damping, n=12 directional — all below the n>=40 trend gate and far below n>=100. Contamination/look-ahead: low (met log ts is intraday, truth is end-of-day resolution); but the join uses the last pre-peak obs so some marine-active rows late in the day already carry near-final info. Recommendation: do NOT wire marine/cirrus damping into the live engine on this evidence; if revived, gate behind n>=100 resolved marine-active city-days. The real finding is the dead plumbing, not a recoverable edge.
